items.title: The cyclic affine type A Cartan datum and its residues
items.statement: Fix e≥2, I=Z/eZ and A with a_ii=2, a_(i,i±1)=−1 for e≥3 and the single double-edge a_01=a_10=−2 for e=2; all d_i=1 and q_i=q. Choose the explicit free lattices P=⊕_i Z Lambda_i⊕Z delta and Pvee=⊕_i Z h_i⊕Z d, with <Lambda_j,h_i>=delta_ij, <delta,h_i>=0, <Lambda_j,d>=0, <delta,d>=1. Define alpha_i=Σ_j a_ji Lambda_j+delta_(i,0) delta. Then the simple roots are independent, Σ_i alpha_i=delta, <h_i,alpha_j>=a_ij, and <d,alpha_i>=delta_(i,0). The central c=Σ_i h_i has <c,alpha_i>=0. Level means <c,weight>; Lambda_i has level1. The symmetric root form has (alpha_i,alpha_j)=a_ij; this is distinct from the lattice pairing. Put P_cl=P/Z delta. The diagram reflection tau fixes Lambda0,delta,d and sends Lambda_i,alpha_i,h_i to the indices−i. The finite vector representation below has level0; its perfect crystal has level1.
items.strategy: The Cartan identities follow from the displayed cycle/double edge. For roots, A has kernel Q·(1,…,1): Σ a_ij x_j=0 implies x constant by the finite sum Σ(x_i−x_(i+1))² (for e=2 use its displayed matrix). A linear relation Σ x_i alpha_i=0 therefore has constant x, and its delta coefficient x0=0 forces all x=0. The chosen pairing is perfect on the explicit bases and the roots/coroots define a valid minimal affine datum of rank e+1. Row sums give delta and c identities. Reflection of the cycle fixes the0 coordinate, so tau preserves all pairings/roots and extends to the full datum. No fundamental weights are silently assumed for an unrelated datum.

items.title: The level-one vector representation, its affinization and the energy function
items.statement: Use j=1,…,e as representatives (j=e represents0). The derived affine vector module V=⊕ Q(q)v_j has K_i v_j=q^(delta_(j≡i)−delta_(j≡i+1))v_j, E_i v_j=delta_(j≡i+1)v_(j−1), F_i v_j=delta_(j≡i)v_(j+1), indices cyclic. Its P_cl weight is Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1), level0; its finite crystal has f_i b_i=b_(i+1), e_i b_(i+1)=b_i, epsilon(b_j)=Lambda_(j−1)^cl and phi(b_j)=Lambda_j^cl, level1. The full affinization has u_(j−ae)=z^a v_j of P-weight Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1)+a delta and K_d eigen q^a. Equivalently E_i(z^a v_j)=delta_(j≡i+1) z^(a+delta_(i,0))v_(j−1), F_i(z^a v_j)=delta_(j≡i) z^(a−delta_(i,0))v_(j+1). Thus E_i u_m=delta_(m≡i+1)u_(m−1), F_i u_m=delta_(m≡i)u_(m+1). Ordinary order is u_m>u_n iff m>n. The energy is explicitly in the OPPOSITE tensor-crystal channel of KMPY bar-Delta-plus (opposite our fixed Delta): H_op(z^a b_j⊗z^b b_k)=chi(j>k)+b−a, and l(z^a b_j)=ae−j. It has the two loop-shift axioms, is constant on that channel's components, is0 on extremal diagonals and H_op>0 iff m1>m2. For a fixed charge M the ground sequence is b°_s=u_(M−s), s≥0: epsilon(b°_s)=phi(b°_(s+1)) and H_op(b°_s,b°_(s+1))=1. It is determined after the initial phase/loop vector (hence charge) is fixed, not independently of an overall loop shift. All statements include e=2.
items.strategy: Check E/F/K on the explicit u_m: each color acts on disjoint pairs (u_(i+ke),u_(i+ke+1)), with K eigen q,q^-1 and zero second powers. Different-color mixed commutators and the cycle Serre sums follow directly from these shifts; the e=2 cubic sums vanish because each squared single-color operator is0. The z-shifts on the0 edge give [d,E0]=E0,[d,F0]=−F0 and the displayed P-weights; forgetting d leaves only P_cl, not a full P-grading on finite V. Compute epsilon/phi from the arrows. KMPY uses b_j^src→b_(j+1) here and its ground indexk→u_(1−k); its MAIN bar-Delta-plus and tensor rule(2.2.13) were visually read. In that OP channel inspect the two-index rule: non-wrap moves do not change chi except at the coincident/adjacent case where the rule selects the other factor, and wrap moves change chi by the opposite of the loop-power change. This proves H_op constancy including the ties/e=2. For m1=j−ae,m2=k−be, the cases b−a positive/zero/negative prove H_op>0 iff m1>m2. The ground identities are the wrap/nonwrap calculation with adjacent integer indices. The bridge lemma later constructs the actual normalized R; no field R property is imported from the unavailable KMN source.

items.title: The vector representation is a perfect crystal of level one and carries a lower global basis
items.statement: The derived level0 vector module has a level1 perfect crystal B={b_1,…,b_e}. Its weights are the finite Weyl orbit of lambda°=Lambda1−Lambda0 in P_cl, with one-dimensional weight spaces and the usual finite highest-weight cone; B⊗B is connected. Every epsilon/phi has level1, B_min=B, and epsilon,phi biject onto the level1 dominant P_cl weights. The basis G(b_j)=v_j, with ordinary semilinear coefficient bar, is an integral/bar-compatible lower basis: all rank-one strings have TWO vertices (highest weight1), their E/F coefficients are1, and divided powers of order≥2 vanish. On V_aff take G(z^a b_j)=z^a v_j with the same properties and the full P-weight; A=Z[q±] and A0 charts are kept separate. The finite V is a U-prime module with P_cl weights, not a level1 full P-graded highest module.
items.strategy: The finite Weyl reflections permute the vector weights Lambda_j−Lambda_(j−1); take the finite subdiagram I\{0} and lambda° for the highest cone. For B⊗B in our convention, any off-diagonal(a,b) can be raised in its FIRST factor by e_(a−1) until a=b: while a≠b, both comparison entries are0, so the non-strict e tie picks the first factor and that arrow exists. Diagonal(j,j) connects to(j+1,j+1) by two f_j moves. This proves connectedness, and the OP channel is its flip. The displayed epsilon/phi are the fundamental-class bijections, proving the level1 perfect conditions; the weights themselves have level0 and are not in W Lambda0. Direct generator matrices prove integral stability, both bar relations and the lower A0 crystal data. All relevant T_(i,c,t) on these integral weights have Gaussian eigenvalues. There is no invocation of highest-module global basis existence for an unbounded level0 affinization.

items.title: The affine Hecke algebra and its commuting action on tensor powers of the vector representation
items.statement: Over Q(q) put Q=q², c=Q−1. Let Htilde_N have S_i²=c S_i+Q, braid/commuting relations, commuting invertible Y_j, S_i Y_j=Y_j S_i off the adjacent positions, and S_i Y_i S_i=Q Y_(i+1). Y_j multiplies the jth loop z, so u_(j−ae)=Y^a v_j; it is NOT z^-1. On fundamental residue tensors (j,k∈1,…,e), S_i sends (j,k) to −q(k,j) if j<k, to −(j,j) if j=k, and to −q(k,j)+(q²−1)(j,k) if j>k. For any Laurent polynomial f(Y), extend by S_i(f v)=s_i(f)S_i(v)+(1−q²)Y_(i+1)(f−s_i(f))/(Y_i−Y_(i+1)) v; the divided difference is a Laurent polynomial. This defines the action on all affine vectors. Equivalently the Leclerc generator t_i=−q^-1 S_i has roots q^-1,−q. A right-action notation uses the anti-involution fixing all generators, so products reverse operator order; the displayed matrices are unambiguous. The action commutes with the fixed U_q action (including total d). Put S_w by reduced words and A_N=Σ_(w∈S_N)S_w.
items.strategy: This is the complete Leclerc§3.3–3.4 action, with S=−q t. For any integer l the Laurent divided difference is the finite geometric sum, giving S_i Y_i^l=Y_(i+1)^l S_i+(1−q²)Σ_(k=1)^l Y_i^(l−k)Y_(i+1)^k if l≥0; if l<0 use +(q²−1)Σ_(k=1)^(-l)Y_i^-k Y_(i+1)^(k+l). These formulas cover every loop shift. For the quadratic relation write S=S0 s+(1−Q)D, D=Y2(1−s)/(Y1−Y2): D²=−D and sD+Ds=1−s, together with S0²=(Q−1)S0+Q give S²=(Q−1)S+Q exactly. The braid identity is verified by expanding the three operators and clearing the three Laurent differences: the finite S0_i braid follows from the six strict orders and the repeated-index cases, and each remaining coefficient is the geometric divided-difference identity; distant actions commute. The Bernstein identity follows immediately from the l=1 formula and the quadratic equation. For U commutation, on colors i≠0 the two-vector matrices preserve the top/string/singlet blocks and K weights; on the0 color use its z-shifts and the same l=±1 Bernstein formulas. Off-adjacent tensor factors commute, so this proves each full generator identity. Total d commutes because each summand preserves total loop degree. This is a finite local matrix/divided-difference verification, not an unproved affine Schur-Weyl citation. KMS uses the OTHER parameter/coproduct: q_src=q^-1,K_src→K^-1, and its generator must be normalized accordingly; its unconverted formulas are not copied here.

items.title: The q-antisymmetrizer splits the tensor power and its kernel is the sum of the Hecke kernels
items.statement: For the displayed H_N(q²) action let C_N=Σ_w q^(2 length(w))=Π_(r=1)^N(1+q²+…+q^(2(r−1))). Then A_N²=C_N A_N and Ker A_N=Σ_i Ker(S_i+1). The field quotient by this kernel is Im A_N. The two-factor kernel is the partial q-symmetric subspace, generated by its explicit loop-shifted U-orbits; its quotient relations are the FULL three-case straightening recurrence in the next Definition. At q=1 these are ordinary antisymmetry. No torsionfree-over-A argument or A0 quotient of Laurent A is used.
items.strategy: Factor A_N on both sides by(1+S_i) using paired Coxeter lengths. Hence S_i A_N=A_N S_i=Q A_N, so A_N²=C_N A_N. Let J=ΣKer(S_i+1); the paired-length factorization gives J⊂Ker A_N. For every x, (S_i−Q)x lies in Ker(S_i+1) because(S_i+1)(S_i−Q)=0. Thus modulo J, x S_w≡Q^length(w)x and x A_N≡C_N x. If A_N x=0 this gives C_N x∈J; C_N≠0 in the generic field proves x∈J. It also proves the splitting/idempotent quotient. For two factors compute S on the three residue cases and the complete l∈Z Bernstein recurrence: equal residues yield symmetric loop relations; unequal residues yield the base adjacent residue relation and its symmetric-loop shifts, whose gap induction is exactly the following three-case recurrence. This establishes the kernel on the ORIGINAL Laurent-loop vector space, not only a localization.

items.title: The finite q-wedge space and the normal-ordering relations
items.statement:
Set wedge^N V_aff=V_aff^tensorN/Ker A_N, with u_(m1)∧…∧u_(mN) its images. Fix normal order m1>…>mN. The quotient is U_q-stable for the fixed coproduct. For l<m write m−l=a e+b, a≥0, 0≤b<e. The exact local relations are: u_l∧u_l=0; u_l∧u_m=−u_m∧u_l if b=0; u_l∧u_m=−q^-1 u_m∧u_l if a=0,b>0; and if a>0,b>0,
u_l∧u_m=−q^-1u_m∧u_l−u_(l+ae)∧u_(m−ae)−q^-1u_(m−ae)∧u_(l+ae).
Repeat this same recurrence on its remaining unordered pair; the gap drops by e in that branch. All correction indices are strictly between l,m, with the same sum and residue multiset. The integral lattice W_A is the image of the Laurent tensor lattice and equals the A-span of the normal basis after the next theorem. The zero chart W0 is separately its A0 normal-basis span; W_A/qW_A is0 and is not a crystal residue. The numerical energy criterion uses H_op from the explicitly OP channel; H_op>0 is equivalent to normal decreasing indices, not a claim about our tensor crystal projector.
items.strategy: Use S=−q t and Leclerc Proposition8. Its full two-factor Bernstein computation gives the displayed three cases, not a truncated sum with constant coefficients. For a>0,b>0, (l+ae,m−ae)=(m−b,l+b) is already decreasing; the third pair is its reverse and has gap ae−b=(a−1)e+(e−b), so repeated application is finite. Equal residues follow from the symmetric loop-shift action on the diagonal kernel; repeated entries vanish. All relations lie in Ker(S+1) and the kernel/gap induction gives generation. U-stability follows from the checked Hecke intertwiners. The later normalized-R bridge proves the exact braiding kernel; it does not replace this finite computation. Integral coefficients are Laurent integers, and positive/infinity crystal charts require separate rings.

items.title: The q-wedge relations coincide with the type-A energy braiding kernel
items.statement:
Put a=Y1/Y2 and let P flip the two tensor factors INCLUDING their loop variables. On the fixed-coproduct affine tensor module define the completed normalized R by the LEFT coefficient formula R_fix=(q²−a)^-1[(a−1)S+q²−1], expanded with psi_fix=1−q²/a. Then R_fix swaps Y1,Y2, fixes every extremal u⊗u, commutes with the fixed U action, and obeys the normalized Yang-Baxter equation. The polynomial-cleared operator has
psi_fix(R_fix−1)=(a^-1−1)(S+1).
Multiplication by a^-1−1 is injective on the original Laurent-loop module, hence its kernel is EXACTLY Ker(S+1) there. Define R_op=P R_fix P, psi_op=1−q²a. This is KMPY's MAIN bar-Delta-plus (OPPOSITE our Delta) channel, with source b_j→our b_(j+1), source ground indexk→u_(1−k). Its q0 leading term is z^H_op b1⊗z^-H_op b2 and psi_op≡1 modq. Its source kernel N_op=P Ker(S+1) is the U_op/symmetric-loop orbit of an extremal diagonal, with C_(j,k)=v_j⊗z^-chi(j>k)v_k+q z^-chi(j>k)v_k⊗v_j (j≠k) and C_(j,j)=v_j⊗v_j. Flip gives the fixed quotient and all its promised R/energy content. It is not asserted that flip identifies the source's A0 descending-wedge chart with our descending chart; that actual chart is proved locally next.
items.strategy: From the Bernstein formula write S=S0 s+(1−q²)Y2(1−s)/(Y1−Y2), with s exchanging loops. Substitution gives R_fix=[(a−1)S0+q²−1]/(q²−a)·s; thus the loop-swap identities are literal and the diagonal S0 eigen−1 gives normalization1. The denominator psi_fix has constant1 atq0, so the geometric q-adic series is legitimate even though a weight space of the affinized tensor can be infinite. Multiplication by loop functions commutes with U-prime, the combination of S and identity intertwines U-prime, and ratios a have total d-degree0; hence R intertwines the full affine module. Keep coefficients LEFT: subtract identity and clear the denominator to get the displayed equality. No original Laurent vector is lost by clearing psi; a^-1−1 is nonzero in the Laurent domain acting freely, proving the stated kernel before localization. For Yang-Baxter, use numerators B_i(x)=(x−1)S_i+(Q−1), Q=q². Expanding B_i(x)B_j(xy)B_i(y), reduce S_i²=(Q−1)S_i+Q and the braid. The coefficients of the eight resulting Hecke words match the opposite expansion because (x−1)(y−1)+(x−1)+(y−1)=xy−1; the scalar denominators are the same commuting product. Loop permutations supply x,y,xy, so this is the completed operator identity. Flip proves the OP statements. Atq0 the OP fundamental cases j>k,j=k,j<k respectively give loop factors a,1,1 before the loop swap, hence H_op=chi(j>k)+secondPower−firstPower; this is an actual matrix calculation, not missing KMN input. The C vectors follow by the l=0,±1 Bernstein formulas and are in the diagonal orbit: two consecutive F moves reach every diagonal, one move gives adjacent C, and continuing around the cycle gives each C with the required0-edge shift. Common loop shifts and symmetric powers Y1^n+Y2^n extend these base cases to every gap; subtract their leading bad pair and induct on the gap as in the full straightening recurrence, proving generation. The source energy/ground/coproduct displays were visually pinned; the native claim that R COMMUTES with individual loops is replaced by the actual SWAP.

items.title: Normally ordered q-wedges form a basis for every finite wedge length
items.statement: For every N, decreasing-index wedges are a field basis and an A=Z[q±] basis of W_A. Straightening terminates using a well-founded pair profile: correction terms strictly decrease dominance of the sorted index multiset, while a leading adjacent swap decreases inversion count. Indices stay inside their original finite bounds; there is no bound by the initial inversion count alone. Define W0=⊕_(normal tuples) A0 u_I, and W_inf its actual bar chart once the normalized bar is constructed; these are not W_A moduloq. W0 with residues of the ordered wedges is a crystal basis of the integrable affine wedge module. The unordered image of the full A0 tensor lattice need not equal W0, and negative q powers in straightening are not falsely called q0-triangular.
items.strategy: Spanning: each relation preserves total index sum and keeps indices in the original finite interval. There are finitely many possible multisets/permutations; every secondary pair is more balanced, lowering the sorted dominance profile, and leading swaps reduce inversions. A repeated entry gives0. Thus all branches terminate. Independence: apply the finite antisymmetrizer to any finite family of decreasing tensors; its Laurent coefficients specialize atq1 to independent ordinary antisymmetrizations, so a nonzero finite minor remains nonzero in Q(q). This proves field independence. Integral Laurent straightening then proves W_A is free with precisely that basis, not by nonPID torsionfreeness. For the crystal claim, fix i and the occupied set of a normal integer tuple. The pairs(i+ke,i+ke+1) are disjoint even at e=2. Empty/doubly occupied pairs are frozen; a singly occupied pair is a two-vertex string. Shifting an index by1 either stays ordered or collides and vanishes, so every finite orbit is a product of these free bits. In decreasing-index order the projected coproduct coefficients are exactly the standard tensor of highest-weight1 strings; frozen double pairs contribute net K weight0. Existing finite rank-one tensor rule proves A0 string stability, partial inverses and the residue basis on every such block. This supplies the correct lower chart without importing a source-chart identification through the OP flip.

items.title: The semi-infinite q-wedge Fock space and its q-adic topology
items.statement: For charge M form the algebraic direct limit of the finite wedge spaces by appending u_(M−N),u_(M−N−1),… to a prefix of length N. Equivalently quotient the eventually-vacuum tensor space by the local wedge kernels. Normal semi-infinite words have i_k=Lambda_k−k+1+M with Lambda a partition, and the vacuum is u_M∧u_(M−1)∧…. Let F_A=⊕_Lambda A|Lambda;M>, F0=⊕ A0|Lambda;M>, F_Z0=⊕ Z[q]|Lambda;M>. The separated q-adic topology uses q^n F0 (or the integral chart), NEVER q^nF_A=F_A. Finite label components complete to Q((q)) tensor_Q(q)F_mu. Fix j(M)∈{1,…,e}, M=j−ae. The vacuum P-weight Omega_M is normalized by Omega0=Lambda0 and Omega_M−Omega_(M−1)=wt(u_M). Explicitly if M=te+r,0≤r<e, Omega_M=Lambda_r−[e t(t−1)/2+t r]delta. A partition's weight is Omega_M−Σ_cells alpha_(content+M), and its size is a separate grading. The Cartan d eigenvalue is Omega_M(d) minus the number of residue0 cells, not partition size. No false Omega_M=Omega_(M−e)+delta periodicity is asserted.
items.strategy: Append the exact ground tail. If a finite word becomes nonnormal across the cutoff, integral straightening stays inside its index interval. A tail filled with every integer in that interval eventually forces any offending term to0; ordered words stabilize to the displayed beta-number partition words. Their independence follows from sufficiently large finite normal-basis independence. Thus the algebraic quotient/direct limit has this basis and Laurent/integral/local charts. In the A0 chart every nonzero finite coordinate has finite valuation, so the topology is separated; completion of a finite-dimensional component is the usual Laurent-series completion. The vacuum weights follow by adding one affine vector u_M; summing its loop power a(M)=(j−M)/e gives the explicit quadratic delta shift. This discharges charge rather than silently changing the full d-action. In charge0 Omega0=Lambda0 and residues remain c−r.

items.title: Tail estimates: q-adic vanishing against the vacuum and finiteness of the weight strings
items.statement: For the fixed type-A ground sequence b°_s=u_(M−s), the source OP energy condition H_op(b⊗b°_s)≤0 means the added integer index lies inside/below the filled right tail. Its wedge with that tail is0, and a sufficiently long finite prefix is already0, hence lies in q^n W0 for every n. The dual left-tail condition has the analogous exact finite vanishing. A nonzero-weight endomorphism C of V_aff commuting with z has only finitely many loop-shift/color terms per fundamental vector; insertion deep in a ground tail is eventually0, hence converges q-adically to0. For the explicit period operator T on F(M), prepend e vacuum entries and shift every old index down e. It preserves each label-weight/size component; on positive size n its kth power is0 when ke>n. Consequently(1−T)^-1=1+T+… is a finite geometric sum on every nonvacuum weight, proving the rationality/isomorphism used in the tail recurrence. Each label weight has finitely many partition vectors. The explicit p(k) highest-component character consequence is established later from the full crystal; it is not an assumed pre-crystal freeness input.
items.strategy: All straightening indices remain between input extremes. For left-tail insertion, once the prefix contains that index, it has r+1 entries in a filled interval with only r available distinct integers, so every normal term vanishes. Reverse the finite interval for the dual statement. For an endomorphism commuting with z, its coefficients/finite shifts are periodic in the e fundamental colors. Nonzero weight excludes an unchanged-index term. Deep insertion changes the total index sum while all entries lie in one completely filled finite interval; an ordered tuple of that cardinality in that interval must be the original vacuum tuple, whose sum differs. Thus every term vanishes after a finite cutoff; no unbounded evaluation statement is imported from8. For T^k, the first ke entries are vacuum and all shifted old entries are≤M once ke>Lambda1. Normal charge-M words with maximal entry≤M are only the vacuum, while total size n>0 is preserved, so T^k=0. This proves the claimed finite inverse on nonvacuum components, stronger than merely formal q-adic injectivity. For finite weights, simple roots are independent in the explicit datum, so a fixed Omega_M−Σ n_i alpha_i fixes sizeΣn_i, and only finitely many partitions have that size. These type-A proofs replace unconverted KMPY tail/display assertions.

items.statement:
Normal charge-M wedges are indexed bijectively by partitions Lambda through i_k=Lambda_k−k+1+M; at M=0 the vacuum is the empty partition. Define the linear endomorphisms by stable finite-prefix action. In charge0,
F_i|lambda>=Σ_(addable gamma resi) q^(A_i^r−R_i^r)|lambda+gamma>,
E_i|mu>=Σ_(removable gamma resi) q^−(A_i^l−R_i^l)|mu−gamma>,
where both counts for E use the SMALLER partition mu−gamma and exclude gamma. All sums are finite. K_i acts by q^(addable_i−removable_i), and K_d by q^−m0(lambda); size|lambda| is separate. items.title: The level-one partition Fock space and node residues
items.statement: Let F=⊕_(partitions lambda) Q(q)|lambda> with its chosen charge0 weight Lambda0−Σ m_i(lambda)alpha_i and size grading. Node(r,c) has residue c−r mod e. The vacuum is empty; F_i adds and E_i removes with the preceding explicit finite node formulas. K_i eigenvalues are proved by the node-count lemma; K_d acts by q^−m0. These are declared linear operators until the affine-relation theorem proves the module structure. A partition is e-regular iff each positive part has multiplicity<e; it is e-restricted iff lambda_r−lambda_(r+1)<e for every r, equivalently its CONJUGATE has part multiplicities<e. A column of height e is allowed in an e-restricted partition. Full Fock/crystal vertices are ALL partitions; the empty component will be the e-regular subset.
items.strategy: Transport the algebraic wedge basis along the proved beta-number bijection. The root/size/d labels and residues are literal corner computations, including the0-edge loop shift. The regular/restricted equivalence follows from lambda_r−lambda_(r+1) being the multiplicity of the column height r in lambda-prime. For example(1^e) is e-restricted but not e-regular. items.title: The addable-minus-removable node count is the level-one Cartan pairing
items.statement: For every partition lambda and every i in I, with N_i(lambda)=I_i(lambda)-R_i(lambda) the number of addable i-nodes minus the number of removable i-nodes of lambda, one has N_i(lambda)=delta_{i,0}-sum_j a_ij m_j(lambda). Consequently sum_i N_i(lambda)=1, the toral operator K_i acts on |lambda> by q^{<h_i,wt(|lambda>)>}=q^{N_i(lambda)}, and the central element K_0K_1...K_{e-1} acts by q, so wt(|lambda>)=Lambda_0-sum_j m_j alpha_j has level 1 and the toral action is the one required for F to be a U_q-module. In particular N_i(empty)=delta_{i,0}, and adding a node of residue k changes N_i by -a_ik, hence changes wt by -alpha_k.
items.strategy: Induct on the number of nodes: the empty partition has one addable node, of residue 0, so N_i(empty)=delta_{i0}. If mu is obtained from lambda by adding a residue-k node, the addable and removable i-node counts change by the standard local rule: the new node appears as a removable i-node only if i=k, and exactly the addable/removable nodes of lambda adjacent along the rim change status; bookkeeping the corners of the skew shape mu/lambda gives N_i(mu)-N_i(lambda)=-a_ik=-(2delta_{ik}-delta_{i,k+1}-delta_{i,k-1}). This is the local form of the identity and iterates from the empty partition. Equivalent formulations are Leclerc Exercise 16 (t_i|lambda>=q^{N_i(lambda)}|lambda> with N_i the addable-minus-removable count) and the standard colored-Young-diagram weight computation of Misra-Miwa sec. 2 (wt(lambda)=Lambda_0-sum m_i alpha_i). The consequence sum_i N_i(lambda)=1 is the row-sum identity of the affine Cartan matrix together with delta_{i0}-sum_j a_ij m_j summing to 1.

items.statement: The constructed node operators on ALL partition vectors give a chosen P-graded integrable U_q(affine sl_e)-module for the fixed coproduct/Cartan datum. items.title: Good and cogood nodes by residue-signature reduction
items.statement: For an i-node word in the fixed INCREASING-content order write+=(addable),−=(removable), cancel adjacent−+ until no such pair remains. Surviving minuses are normal REMOVABLE nodes and the FIRST surviving minus is the good node for e_i; surviving pluses are conormal ADDABLE nodes and the LAST surviving plus is the cogood node for f_i. Missing chosen sign means the operator is0. Equivalently read DECREASING content/columns (top-to-bottom), cancel+−, take good=LAST− and cogood=FIRST+. These name conventions match the usual Fayers good deletion/cogood addition. They are combinatorial string data, not a selection by minimum ordinary Chevalley exponent.
items.strategy: Unique reduction follows by the stack matching of−+; any two local deletions commute or share no cancellable pair, so the matching survivors do not depend on deletion order. Reverse the word to obtain+− with first/last exchanged. The fixed-residue cube supplies the actual operator interpretation and both endpoints; no existence/module assertion is needed in this Definition. At e3 lambda2,i2 the two pluses choose the top-right cell(1,3), not the native leftmost opening at(2,1). At lambda21,i2 the minus-plus pair cancels; F2|21> may be nonzero but tilde f2 is0. items.title: The crystal of the level-one Fock space is the good-node partition graph
items.statement: The WHOLE level-one Fock module has the crystal basis(F0,B_F), F0=⊕_(ALL partitions)A0|lambda>, B_F={|lambda>+qF0}. The actual normalized Kashiwara operators REMOVE the good normal i-node and ADD the cogood conormal i-node of the corrected signature; epsilon/phi are survivor counts. This is a graph on ALL partitions, not only regular ones. Its empty connected component is precisely the e-regular partitions; e-restricted labels belong to the transposed model. A pole or a unique Chevalley term does not determine the crystal arrow.
items.strategy: Each fixed-residue block is the finite tensor bit module of the local cube supplier, so its raw A0 basis is stable under string operators and has the stated residue rule, including both endpoints. The full module is generated over the field by this free weight-graded lattice and satisfies the quantum relations; all crystal axioms follow blockwise and the weight formula is the node-count lemma. To identify the empty component, use DECREASING-content order. Removing the selected LAST minus could violate regularity only if it creates e equal rows of lengthL−1; then below its removable row lies a block of e−1 rows of lengthL−1 and their last corner is a consecutive same-residue minus. If the upper minus survives so does this lower one, so the upper one cannot be selected. Adding the FIRST plus could violate regularity only if a block of e−1 rows of the new length lies immediately above it; that block's first addable corner is a consecutive same-residue plus. If the lower plus survives the earlier one does too, so it is not selected. Thus both operators preserve e-regularity. Every nonempty regular partition has a top equal-row block of heighta<e; its first removable corner has residueL−a, while the only earlier addable corner has residueL, so its minus has no matching same-residue plus and survives. Some good deletion therefore exists, remains regular and lowers size. Induction and the inverse axiom reach every regular partition from empty. Since empty is regular and all adjacent edges preserve regularity, this proves exactly the component, without an abstract rank-one recognition assumption or an imported MM path count.

items.title: The empty component is the highest weight crystal B(Lambda_0)
items.statement: With the declared AC for the general integrable-module decomposition, the empty component of the full partition crystal is the canonical B(Lambda0), with exactly the e-regular labels. Its module is M=U_q|empty> and its lower A0 lattice is M∩F0. It occurs once. More precisely F=⊕_(k≥0)V(Lambda0−k delta)^⊕p(k), a LOCALLY WEIGHT-FINITE indexed direct sum, where p(k) counts ordinary partitions of k. Hence chF=chV(Lambda0)Π_(r≥1)(1−exp(−r delta))^-1. A highest CRYSTAL label need not be a highest FIELD standard vector; the ambient canonical basis need not split these summands.
items.strategy: The full Fock module has finite label spaces and supportLambda0−Q+; its full crystal basis was proved from cubes. Apply the actual7 top-isotypic lattice/residue splitting and indexed decomposition. The highest weightLambda0 space is1-dimensional with vacuum, so its isotypic submodule is the simple M of the preceding proposition and its component is the canonical B(Lambda0); the direct combinatorial proof gives the regular labels. For all other highest vertices, inspect boundary signs by top-to-bottom decreasing content: for the top block of a equal rows of lengthL, the only earlier plus has residueL and its removable minus has residueL−a. If all minuses are canceled, a must be divisible by e. Cancel this block's matching pair and repeat with each next block. Conversely every block with multiplicity divisible by e pairs its own plus/minus, so all e_i residues vanish. Thus highest labels are exactly partitions formed by repeating each row of an ordinary partition rho e times. Each residue occurs|rho| times, giving weightLambda0−|rho|delta; there arep(k) such labels. The decomposition theorem identifies their field constituents and multiplicities, giving the full formula/character. This does not call those raw standard vectors field-highest. AC is used only through the already-declared decomposition/top-lift selection; all finite sign computations are choice-free.

items.title: The regular-partition label convention and the Mullineux crystal involution
items.statement: Regular means multiplicity<e; restricted means adjacent differences<e. Conjugation C:lambda→lambda-prime is a comparison between the regular and restricted MODELS and sends residuei to−i. It is NOT the same-model sign/Mullineux map. On the regular basic crystal define M by negating all colors of any lowering path from empty: M(f_i b)=f_(-i)M(b), M(empty)=empty. This is a well-defined involution INSIDE the regular label set, and wtM=tau(wt), with tau(alpha_i)=alpha_-i, tauLambda0=Lambda0, taudelta=delta; there is no affine longest w0 formula. The restricted sign involution is C M C^-1. Dominance on equal-size partitions is the published prefix-sum order, reversed by conjugation; horizontal-strip inclusion is not dominance.
items.strategy: The elementary node transpose reverses content and preserves addable/removable polarity; the corrected regular/restricted signatures are mirrored exactly. For M, use the explicit datum reflectiontau. It preserves all defining Serre/toral relations and the highest relations ofLambda0. The early universal simple quotient therefore has a field-linear semilinear-in-U operatorJ_tau sending a divided word v to the word with colors negated; tau²=1 makes its square identity. The A0 lattice is generated by lower words and J_tau commutes with the string operators with relabeled colors, so it gives a genuine involution on its crystal. The proved empty-component identification transports it to regular partition labels. This proves path independence, bijection and weight action; conjugation merely transports that involution to the other model. For e2 tau is the identity, while conjugation generally changes a regular partition into a restricted one, visibly distinguishing the maps. Invoke the actual dominance Definition for the last assertion, not a made-up strip gloss.

items.title: The basic representation global basis is unitriangular in the partition basis
items.statement: There is an explicit semi-infinite wedge bar psi, with the vacuum fixed, q→q^-1 and U/bar compatibility. Its restriction to M is the normalized highest-module bar. On ALL partitions its integral triangular correction gives G(lambda)=|lambda>+Σ_(mu strictly dominated bylambda) d_(mu,lambda)(q)|mu>, with d inqZ[q], diagonal1 and same e-core support. The full family is an A-basis of the partition Laurent lattice and an A0 basis, with actual infinity chartpsiF0 and balanced Z intersection. Exactly the e-regular G(lambda) form the lower global basis of M, identified by the two actual8 lower-global suppliers. The ambient basis is not automatically compatible with the other field irreducible summands. The native equality d_(lambda,mu)=d_(mu-prime,lambda-prime) for ALL lower coefficients is FALSE; LT's transpose statement concerns the BAR matrix, not D. Ambient natural-form dual coefficients use(D^-1)^t; basic upper coefficients require the restricted Gram inverse and need not be Laurent polynomials.
items.strategy: Finite normalized bar on a raw lengthr wedge is psi_r(u_I)=(-1)^(r(r−1)/2)q^t(I)u_reverseI, t(I)=#pairs of UNEQUAL residues of the actual indices. Verify it preserves the full two-factor kernel by the three-case Bernstein/straightening recurrence; residue multiset is preserved, so the global factor is compatible. Applying twice gives1. For F_i shifting one top residue to the next, t(I+)−t(I)=n_i−n_(i+1)−1; its exponent after q-conjugating the prefix exactly equals the reversed suffix exponent. The analogous E change is−(n_i−n_(i+1))−1. These explicit color-count identities prove finite U/bar compatibility; no unavailable quasi-R action is used. Leading reversal/swap factors cancel to diagonal1; every secondary pair balances the sorted indices and strictly decreases dominance, preserving residue multiset. Thus psi_r is integral and dominance triangular. For truncation, choose m≥partition size and all prefix indices>−m. Move the new minimum u_-m through the prefix. Every secondary correction removes that minimum and leaves all(m+1) indices>−m; their sum is ground_sum_m+size−m≤ground_sum_m, while the minimum sum of(m+1) DISTINCT integers>−m isground_sum_m+1. Bounded-index straightening therefore kills every secondary branch. Only the leading (-1)^m q^-#unequal factor remains, exactly canceling the new normalization. This proves actual prefix independence and separated-chart limits, not an author obligation. For E/F compatibility in Fock choose a large prefix avoiding the relevant color at the artificial tail boundary; the scalar is then1 and no boundary term survives, so the finite compatibility passes to the limit. Each degree is finite. Solve the finite triangular semilinear system: residualf obeys f+barf=0; its unique positive-q part gives the next correction. This gives d∈qZ[q], uniqueness, all Laurent/local bases and the Z-balanced intersection. Same-core support follows because every local recurrence preserves the beta-number residues: at a large fixed prefix the packed runner counts determine a unique abacus core; sliding a bead by e into a vacancy removes a rim e-strip and decreases total degree, so packing terminates uniquely and depends only on those counts. On M, its A-lattice maps into the partition A-lattice because all divided node matrices are Laurent-integral (cube proof); its lower lattice maps into F0 and the actual8 global lifts are bar fixed. Their regular crystal residues identify their images with the unique ambient G by balanced uniqueness. Hence every regular G is genuinely in M, without assuming an integral splitting or saturation. Field perfectness/form-duality is standard-partition orthonormal by the node polarization identity; lower M_A need not be A-selfdual. The false D-transpose equality is already refuted at e2 degree4: d_(211,4)=q but d_(1111,31)=0. Actual lower/upper functions retain the correct inverse/Gram rules; source LT3.3(iv) is contextual BAR symmetry, not an imported proof of D symmetry.

items.title: Fixed-residue node cubes realize the actual Fock strings
items.statement: For the declared charge0 node operators, fix i and one partition. The orbit obtained by toggling its addable/removable i-cells is a FINITE BOOLEAN cube: availability of one such cell is unchanged by every other i-toggle, including e2. Put the slots in DECREASING content order, state+=addable/top and state−=removable/bottom. The node operators on this cube are exactly V(1)^tensor k for the FIXED rank-one coproduct, with K=q^(#plus−#minus). Its raw A0 partition span is therefore stable under the actual normalized string operators. In that order cancel +−, take f FIRST surviving+, e LAST surviving−; equivalently in the fixed increasing-content order cancel−+, take f LAST+, e FIRST−. Residue labels are all cube vertices, both endpoints are included, and epsilon/phi are the surviving minus/plus counts. The standard partition-orthonormal form is the normalized rank-one polarization, and all divided E/F powers have Laurent-integral matrices. No Chevalley minimum argument is used.
items.strategy: A corner's addability/removability is determined solely by its horizontal/vertical neighbors, whose residues are i±1 and never i for e≥2. Toggling another i-cell does not change any such neighbor, nor creates a new i-slot. Every subset of the finite slots can therefore be toggled, giving all2^k distinct partition diagrams. With slots decreasing in content, the iterated DeltaF coefficient at slotj is q^sum_(slots beforej)weight and the DeltaE coefficient is q^−sum_(slots afterj)weight; these are precisely N_r and−N_l of the node formula because other slots are unchanged. Hence the map from tensor bit vectors to partitions is a rank-one module isomorphism. Apply the already-proved rank-one tensor crystal theorem; its strict f/non-strict e rule unrolls to the stated cancellation/extremes, including zero endpoints. This proves exact A0 stability before any congruence is transported. Divided coproducts give Laurent Gaussian/integer matrices on these fundamental bit factors. For polarization, (F_i lambda,mu)=q^Nr, whereas sigma(F_i)=q^-1 K_i E_i givesq^(N_i(lambda)−1−Nl)=q^Nr; K is self-adjoint. Thus the standard delta Gram is the normalized form, with local perfectness; field and crystal operators are distinguished.

items.title: Integrable rank-one actions force the quantum Serre sums
items.statement: Suppose chosen type-one Cartan/E/F operators satisfy all toral and mixed [E_i,F_j] relations, with each single-color action integrable. Then BOTH quantum Serre sums of order n=1−a_ij hold, including cubic affine e2. This theorem uses no already-imposed Serre relation.
items.strategy: Use the fixed rank-one Hopf action on Hom(W,W-prime). For a finite U_i-submodule W and F_j(W), let W-prime be its finite U_i-envelope; it is finite because every vector in an integrable generic rank-one module lies in a finite string module. The restricted operator F_j has adjoint K weightm=−a_ij and is killed by adjoint E_i: adE(T)=(E_iT−TE_i)K_i, so the mixed commutator gives0. Thus it is a highest vector in the finite integrable Hom module, and adF^(m+1) F_j=0 there by the finite rank-one string theorem. Since W contains any chosen vector, this is an operator identity on the whole module. In our coproduct adF(T)=F_i T−K_i T K_i^-1 F_i. Induction with the Gaussian Pascal formula gives adF^n F_j=Σ_r(−1)^r q_i^(r(m−n+1))[n choose r]_i F_i^(n−r)F_jF_i^r. The induction coefficients are q_i^r[n r]+q_i^(r−n−1)[n,r−1]=[n+1,r]. At n=m+1 the exponent is0, exactly the negative Serre sum. Apply the unsigned Chevalley interchange E↔F,K↔K^-1 to get the positive sum. This is the complete KMPY AppendixB finite-Hom proof transported to our coproduct, not its omitted locally-finite lemma as an assumption.

items.title: Node actions for partitions of size at most three
items.statement: Work out the node formulas of item 12 on all partitions of size at most three for e=2 and e=3. For e=2: F_0|empty>=|1>, E_0|1>=|empty>, F_1|1>=|1,1>, and F_0|2>=|2,1>+q^{-1}|1,1,1> with E_0|2,1>=q^{-2}|1,1>, matching Leclerc Exercise 15; the toral eigenvalues are N_0(empty)=1, N_1(empty)=0, N_0(1)=0, N_1(1)=1, N_0(2)=0, N_1(2)=2, and K_0K_1 acts by q on every partition. For e=3 the same computation lists, for each partition of size at most three, the addable and removable nodes with their residues, the exponents N^r_i,N^l_i and the resulting nonzero coefficients; the good node at q=0 is singled out in each case. All coefficients are computed from the residues c-r mod e of the nodes, and the example verifies that the level-one toral action and the node exponents agree.
items.strategy: Enumerate the addable and removable nodes of each partition and apply the residue rule c-r mod e; order the i-nodes by content and compute N^r_i,N^l_i as in item 15; apply the node formulas of item 12 and, where the partition has several nodes of one residue, compare the exponents to exhibit the good/cogood selection of item 18. The e=2 values are checked against Leclerc Exercise 15 and LT sec. 2; the e=3 values are the first cases of the e-regular/e-restricted dictionary of item 21. items.title: The double-edge Serre cancellation in affine A_1 on partitions
items.statement: For e=2 the adjacency value is a_01=-2, so the quantum Serre relation is cubic: E_0^3E_1-[3]E_0^2E_1E_0+[3]E_0E_1E_0^2-E_1E_0^3=0 and similarly with E and F exchanged. The example evaluates the four compositions on the partitions |empty>, |1>, |2>, |1,1> and verifies the cancellation chain by chain: on |empty> only E_1E_0^3 survives and its coefficient is zero because there is no chain of three removable 0-nodes and one removable 1-node from the empty partition, while on |2> and |1,1> the chains pair as (E_0^3E_1, E_0^2E_1E_0) and (E_0E_1E_0^2, E_1E_0^3) with q-exponents summing to the [3]-multiples, leaving zero. The analogous F-computation on |3>, |2,1>, |1,1,1> exhibits the same cancellation with q^{-1} exponents; in particular F_0 and F_1 do not commute on the partition model although the relation is not the quadratic one.
items.strategy: Compute the node words for residues 0 and 1 on each of the listed partitions, use the exponents of item 15 to expand each of the four compositions, and cancel the paired chains as in the signed involution of LT sec. 3 (the double-edge case is KMS sec. 1.1 relations (9)-(10) and KMPY sec. 5.2.1 with a_01=-2). The surviving terms are collected and shown to vanish exactly because [3]=[2]+q+q^{-1} in the two surviving configurations. This is the e=2 case of item 16 and is the smallest nontrivial quantum Serre check on the Fock space.

items.title: The good-node crystal component of the empty partition for e=3
items.statement: For e=3 list the first three levels of the component of the empty partition in the good-node crystal graph: |empty> with residues of addable and removable nodes, then the partitions of size 1 and 2 reachable by good nodes, with the good and cogood nodes displayed for each partition and each residue 0,1,2. The resulting component is the beginning of the crystal B(Lambda_0) of U_q(ŝl_3), with weights Lambda_0, Lambda_0-alpha_i+delta-terms and the correct multiplicities; the example also exhibits a partition of size 3 outside the component, with its own good-node arrows, showing that the whole Fock crystal is strictly larger than B(Lambda_0). In particular the 3-regular partitions appearing at these levels are exactly the labels of the basic representation, and the non-3-regular partitions which appear at size 3 are not in the component.
items.strategy: Apply the good/cogood signature reduction of item 18 to the node word of each partition and compute the covering arrows; compare with the weights of the highest weight crystal B(Lambda_0) using eps(b)=0 and phi(b)=Lambda_0^cl at the empty partition and the tensor-free rank-one strings of each residue. The outside-component witness is verified by checking that its good-node chain never reaches the empty partition (equivalently, it is not 3-regular). Sources: Misra-Miwa sec. 4 (Prop. 4.3 and Theorem 4.7), Fayers sec. 2 (Theorem 2.1), Leclerc sec. 3.14.

items.title: Unitriangular global basis elements at small rank
items.statement: Compute the global basis expansions for e=2 and small degree: G(empty)=|empty>, G(1)=|1>, G(1,1)=|1,1>, G(2)=|2>+q|1,1>, G(2,1)=|2,1>+q|1,1,1> up to the normalization fixed by G(lambda)=|lambda> mod qL, and the dominance-unitriangular matrices of Leclerc Exercise 17 and LT sec. 4. The example verifies that the entries lie in Z[q,q^{-1}], that off-diagonal entries vanish unless the dominance and e-core conditions hold, and that the transpose symmetry d_{lambda mu}(q)=d_{mu' lambda'}(q) holds on the displayed range; it also identifies the e-regular labels (empty, |1>, |2>, |1,1,1> at low degree for e=2) as the global basis of the basic representation, and shows a bar-fixed vector outside the component whose expansion is not compatible with the component decomposition.
items.strategy: Compute the bar involution by the straightening recursion of item 22 on the displayed partitions, normalize so that G(lambda)=|lambda> mod qL, and record the resulting coefficients; the small-rank matrices are Leclerc Exercise 17 and LT sec. 4 (their matrices are the ones for the charge-zero component after the q<->q^{-1} renormalization, which the example states explicitly). The dominance and core restrictions are checked entry by entry, and the conjugation symmetry is the LT Theorem 3.3(iv) symmetry. The non-regular labels are exhibited as bar-fixed vectors lying outside the empty component, in agreement with the LT remark that the ambient canonical basis is not compatible with the component decomposition.

items.title: The whole partition Fock space is not the basic representation
items.statement: The partition Fock space F is strictly larger than the basic representation M=U_q|empty>: the one-dimensional space spanned by |1^e> (the column of e nodes, which is not e-regular) is not contained in M, and F decomposes as oplus_{k>=0} M(Lambda_0-k delta)^{oplus p(k)}, so the multiplicity of the basic representation in F is one and the higher components are nonzero. In particular no map identifies the whole Fock space with B(Lambda_0), the ambient global basis {G(lambda)} for non-e-regular lambda does not form the global basis of a single highest weight module, and the bar-fixed vector G(1^e) is not a global basis vector of the basic representation.
items.strategy: The column |1^e> has e nodes in one column, all of distinct residues 0,1,...,e-1, and is not e-regular; by the e-regular description of the empty component (item 20, Misra-Miwa Prop. 4.3 and Theorem 4.7) it lies outside the component of the empty partition. The decomposition of the classical Fock space into oplus_k M(Lambda_0-k delta)^{oplus p(k)} (with p the partition function) is the classical decomposition, valid also for the q-deformed Fock space, and is computed by KMS sec. 2.1-2.3 via the Heisenberg algebra: F(m) is isomorphic as U'_q x H-module to V_{Lambda_m} tensor C[H^-], whose U'_q-component is the basic representation and whose grading gives the multiplicities p(k) (Leclerc Prop. 12; LT sec. 1 equation (1)). The statement about the ambient global basis is the LT remark following Theorem 4.1 and the last sentence of item 22.
